title: Why the War Boys Spray Their Mouths with Chrome Before They Die

beats.narration_line: Why would someone spray silver paint into their mouth just before dying?
beats.visual_description: Extreme close-up of Morsov spraying aerosol chrome directly across his open mouth and teeth.

beats.narration_line: In the wasteland of Mad Max, the War Boys don’t fear death—they worship it. Conditioned under Immortan Joe, they believe dying in his service guarantees eternal glory in Valhalla.
beats.visual_description: Immortan Joe standing atop the Citadel balcony in transparent armor, thousands of pale War Boys looking up in divine reverence.

beats.narration_line: The chrome spray isn't madness. To the War Boys, machines are immortal, and chrome is sacred metal. By painting their mouths silver, they turn from mortal flesh into mechanical weapons.
beats.visual_description: War Boys holding the chrome V8 steering wheel idol inside the roaring vehicle, silver teeth shining in harsh desert sunlight.

beats.narration_line: Their desperate cry—'Witness me'—transforms suicide into a celebrated public performance.
beats.visual_description: Morsov raising twin explosive thundersticks, shouting 'Witness me!', other War Boys screaming back 'Witness!'.

beats.narration_line: Immortan Joe’s true power isn’t weapons or water. It’s psychological enslavement. He convinced dying men that their exploitation was supreme honor.
beats.visual_description: Colossal armada of spiked war machines charging across desert sand dunes, young soldiers swaying on poles into destruction.

beats.narration_line: That’s the terrifying part. Immortan Joe doesn’t just command an army willing to die for him. He creates an army that believes dying for him is a reward.
beats.visual_description: Morsov leaping into the enemy vehicle, massive fiery explosion consuming the screen, final frame of ecstatic chrome-covered smile.
